title: Fried Vermicelli / Mee Siam
description: Our Char Kway Teow flavours with rice vermicelli, using Spam or thin beef steaks.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of fried rice vermicelli with chicken, egg and basil.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · chicken and basil variation · displayed crop
personalNote: Same sauce and vegetables as our Char Kway Teow, Jack, but we’re using the thin rice vermicelli this time. We can use thin beef steaks instead of Spam if that’s what we fancy.
equipment: Two containers for the next day’s lunches
advancePrep: Soak the rice vermicelli in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain. If you forgot, use boiling water for 1 minute instead. The hot-water shortcut makes the noodles a bit softer. Get the other ingredients ready while they soak.
importantNotes: This makes dinner for both of us and two lunches for tomorrow. Everything in our Char Kway Teow sauce and vegetable mix stays the same. Get it all ready before heating the wok. The times are estimates and don’t include soaking. If we swap Spam for beef, start with 5 minutes on high heat for a good brown sear; you can cook it for up to 10 minutes if you want it more thoroughly cooked.

ingredients.name: Spam
ingredients.note: Cut into strips, or swap for thinly sliced beef steaks.

ingredients.name: Pak choi
ingredients.note: About 1 pack; separate the leaves and cut the stalks into matchsticks.

ingredients.name: Chives
ingredients.note: Chop; garlic chives are even better if you have them.

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.note: Ready to crack straight into the wok.

ingredients.name: Belachan chilli paste
ingredients.note: Adds a hawker-centre flavour; leave it out if you do not have it.

steps.title: Get everything ready
steps.description: Okay Jack, get everything ready before the wok goes on. Drain the soaked vermicelli, slice the Spam into strips and chop the garlic semi-finely. Separate the pak choi leaves and cut the stalks into matchsticks. Chop the chives and have the beansprouts and eggs beside you. Once we start, this moves quite quickly.
steps.tip: Once the wok is hot, the cooking moves quickly. Finish all the preparation first.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.description: Mix the dark soy, light soy and oyster sauce in a little bowl. If we have belachan chilli paste, add it too—it gives us that hawker-centre flavour. If we don’t, leave it out. Keep the hot water measured separately.

steps.title: Brown our Spam, or sear the beef
steps.description: If we’re using Spam, brown it in the hot wok on high heat for about 3–5 minutes, turning the strips so as many sides as possible get seared. If we’re using thin beef steaks instead, give them 5 minutes on high heat for a good brown sear. You can keep cooking for up to 10 minutes if you want them more thoroughly cooked. Keep turning and checking so they don’t burn.
steps.doneness: Brown, seared edges on several sides.
steps.tip: The timer is a check, Jack. Look at the meat as well; Spam wants browned edges, and the beef wants a good sear and to be cooked how you’re comfortable with it.

steps.title: Fry the garlic
steps.description: Add the garlic and fry it for 1 minute, squishing it around so it doesn’t sit in one hot spot. Browning is fine, but don’t let it go black.
steps.doneness: Garlic smells fragrant and may be lightly browned, but is not black.
steps.warning: Watch the garlic closely because it can burn quickly.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.description: Crack in the eggs and scramble them around with the Spam and garlic until they’re set.

steps.title: Add the noodles and vegetables
steps.description: Now add the drained vermicelli, pak choi leaves and stalks, beansprouts and chives. Use our two wooden spoons to lift and toss everything around for 1 minute so it gets properly mixed.
steps.doneness: The noodles and vegetables are mixed through the Spam and eggs.

steps.title: Add the sauce and finish
steps.description: Pour in the sauce and the measured hot water. Toss it around and cook for about 5 minutes, until the vermicelli are cooked but still have a nice chew. Serve our dinner straight away, and put the two lunch portions aside to cool promptly.
steps.doneness: Cooked noodles with a pleasant chew, coated in the sauce.
steps.tip: Keep the two lunch portions aside for prompt cooling and refrigeration.

substitutions.title: Thin beef steaks instead of Spam
substitutions.text: We can use thinly sliced beef steaks instead of the Spam. Give them 5 minutes on high heat for a good brown sear. If you’re not confident they’re cooked through, cook for up to 10 minutes, keeping an eye on them so they don’t burn. Use the Spam ingredient list for our usual version, or the beef we’re swapping it for.

substitutions.title: Oyster sauce
substitutions.text: Use oyster sauce or vegetarian oyster sauce.

substitutions.title: Chives
substitutions.text: Ordinary chives work; garlic chives are even better if you have them.

substitutions.title: No belachan chilli paste?
substitutions.text: Leave it out. It adds that hawker-centre flavour, but the recipe works without it.

troubleshooting.title: A little softer than you wanted?
troubleshooting.text: Use the 30-minute cold-water soak next time, Jack. The 1-minute boiling-water shortcut makes the vermicelli a little softer.

storage: Divide the two lunch portions into small containers so they cool quickly. Refrigerate within 1–2 hours, keep the fridge at 0–5°C, and eat them for lunch the next day.
reheating: Reheat only the portion you will eat, until steaming hot throughout. Stir during reheating, especially in a microwave, to avoid a cold centre. Reheat only once.
foodSafety: Keep the lunch portions chilled until you are ready to eat or reheat them. Storage and reheating guidance follows the Food Standards Agency’s advice on chilling food and using leftovers.
servingSuggestion: Serve two portions straight from the wok; save the other two for the next day’s lunches.
